titleDv: ޤާނޫނު ނަންބަރު 10/2011 (މުދަލާއި ޚިދުމަތުގެ އަގުން ޓެކްސް ނެގުމުގެ ޤާނޫނު) އަށް ... ވަނަ އިޞްލާޙު ގެނައުމުގެ ބިލު
summary: This government bill amends the Goods and Services Tax Act (Law 10/2011). It ends the tourism GST that has applied since 1 October 2026 to inbound tourism products (accommodation, food, transport and other tourist activities in the Maldives) sold by businesses with no permanent place of business in the Maldives, and to agency or booking services linked to them. GST already collected on these sales since 1 October 2026 would be refunded. The bill also adds a new anti-avoidance rule that lets the Commissioner General of MIRA disregard deals made mainly to get a GST benefit and adjust the tax owed.
whyItMatters: Overseas online travel agents and foreign tour operators would stop charging Maldives tourism GST on these sales. The government's cost sheet, citing MIRA, puts the lost revenue at MVR 1,608.5 million.
keyProvisions: Removes the provisions added for this tax: the item in Article 15 that makes inbound tourism products from businesses without a permanent place of business in the Maldives taxable, the Article 15 clause that started the tax on 1 October 2026, and linked items in Articles 5-2 and 13. It also repeals the Article 19 pricing rule and the Article 37 bar on input tax for these suppliers, and the definition of 'inbound tourism product' in Article 68.

Section 11 stops the tax once the amendment takes effect. GST collected on these products since 1 October 2026 must be refunded to the person it was collected from, and suppliers need not complete any further steps under the Act for that period.

Adds Article 63-1 on GST avoidance. A transaction counts as avoidance if someone got a tax benefit from it and, judged by its substance, getting that benefit was the sole or main reason for it. The Commissioner General may then treat it as unacceptable for tax purposes or void, and change the tax payable, refunds or input tax of any registered person affected, even one who did not take part.

Article 63-1 defines 'transaction' and 'tax benefit' broadly, including paying less GST, claiming more input tax, getting a refund sooner, paying GST later, or making taxable goods or services look non-taxable.

Rewrites Article 59-1 so MIRA can order registered persons to hand over information showing whether anyone required to register for GST has done so, not only tourism suppliers. Article 19 also gets a new item (5) covering goods and services sold to persons other than associated persons.
Regulations must be amended or made and published within 90 days, and the amendment takes effect once it is passed, ratified and published in the Government Gazette.
whoIsAffected: Overseas online travel agents and foreign tour operators selling Maldives tourism services, the tourists who buy from them, GST-registered businesses whose deals could be treated as avoidance, and state revenue.
statedReasons: The government says it wants to stop the GST charged since 1 October 2026 on inbound tourism products and related agency or booking services provided by persons without a permanent place of business in the Maldives. It also wants to strengthen the measures MIRA can take against people who avoid GST.
